_comment: Secrets inventory (F09, #35). Names and metadata only: NEVER values. Validated by scripts/secrets_check.py; docs/ops/config-matrix.md and docs/runbooks/secrets.md embed generated tables.

core-service.description: FastAPI core service on Fly.io, one app per environment (ADR 0003)

ci-deploy.description: GitHub Actions deploy and migration jobs; one GitHub environment per environment

job-tick-function.description: Appwrite Function that ticks the job runner (ADR 0002)

firebase-console.description: Provider-held credential, configured by the owner in a console

app-parent.description: Flutter parent app build (public client keys only)

app-teacher.description: Flutter teacher app build (public client keys only)

app-admin.description: Next.js admin dashboard (ADR 0004); holds no API key, acts as the signed-in admin

local-dev.description: A developer's laptop; sandbox credentials only, never production or staging

codemagic.description: Codemagic CI/CD for the Flutter apps (M01 / release tickets); not yet set up, owner-blocked

app-stores.description: Google Play Console and Apple Developer / App Store Connect signing material; owner-blocked

appwrite-api-key: In the Appwrite console of THIS environment's project (never another), create a new API key with the same scopes as appwrite/keys.md, name it hs-<consumer>-<env>-<yyyymmdd>, expiry 90d.

Set the new value in the store listed for that environment (Fly: `fly secrets import -a <app>` with `APPWRITE_API_KEY=<value>` on stdin (from a mode-600 file you delete afterwards); GitHub: environment secret). Fly restarts machines one at a time, so the old key keeps serving until each machine has the new one.
Verify: GET /health/ready on the app is 200 and one authenticated request succeeds; for CI, re-run the staging deploy workflow.
Delete the OLD key in the Appwrite console (this is the revoke step; on a leak do it as soon as step 3 passes, target within one hour).
Run `python3 appwrite/check_keys.py`, update appwrite/keys.md if scopes or names changed, and add a line to the rotation log (date, who, secret name, environment; no values).
job-tick-secret: Generate a new random value (`openssl rand -hex 32`) locally; never paste it into chat or an issue.

Set it on the core service first (`fly secrets import -a hs-core-<env>` with `JOB_TICK_SECRET=<value>` on stdin), then on the job-tick function variable in the same environment's Appwrite project, then redeploy the function. Until the function has the new value, ticks signed with the old value are rejected and retried on the next tick (ADR 0002 jobs are idempotent), so there is no data loss; a brief gap of one tick is the worst case. F04 has no previous-secret mechanism today, so rotation is NOT fully overlapping; accepting a previous value during rotation is an F04 follow-up (see docs/ops/secrets.md).
Verify: the next tick appears in the job-run log with status ok.
Unset any previous-secret value and record the rotation in the log.
provider-key: In the provider's dashboard for THIS environment (sandbox account for development and staging, live account only for production) create a second key; do not delete the first yet.
Set the new value in the store listed for that environment (`fly secrets import -a <app>` with `NAME=<value>` on stdin; rolling restart, no downtime).
Verify with the provider's smoke call in the staging runbook (send a test message / sandbox request) and that error rates in Sentry stay flat for 15 minutes.
Revoke the OLD key in the provider dashboard (this is the revoke step; on a leak do it immediately after step 3).
Add a line to the rotation log (date, who, secret name, environment; no values).
payment-credential: Stop payouts for the environment by hand so no disbursement is in flight: in the admin app do not approve any payout batch until step 5 (collections keep working because they are retried by provider callbacks). If the DISBURSEMENT credential is the leaked one, revoke it at the provider first. The core service has no automatic payout switch today (payout ticket follow-up).

In the provider portal create a new API user key / secret for THIS environment (sandbox for development and staging; live only for production). MoMo: new API key for the existing API user, or a new API user if the user id is suspect.
Set the new values in the store (`fly secrets import -a hs-core-<env>` with `NAME=<value>` on stdin); machines restart one at a time.
Verify with one sandbox (or, in production, the smallest live) collection and, for disbursement credentials, one payout; confirm callbacks reach the service.
Revoke the OLD credential in the provider portal, resume approving payout batches, and reconcile the ledger for the window between steps 1 and 5 (ADR on idempotent payouts).
Add a line to the rotation log. In production, rotate in a low-traffic window (not weekdays 15:00-20:00 or weekends 08:00-18:00, SR NFR-5).
webhook-secret: In the provider dashboard create a new webhook signing secret for THIS environment; most providers allow two active secrets during a window, so keep the old one.
Set the new value on the core service (`fly secrets import -a hs-core-<env>` with `NAME=<value>` on stdin); the service must verify against the new value.
Trigger a test webhook from the provider and confirm it verifies (HTTP 200, no signature errors in logs).
Remove the old signing secret at the provider.
Add a line to the rotation log.
fly-token: Create a new app-scoped deploy token: `fly tokens create deploy -a hs-core-<env> -x 2160h` (90 days).
Replace the GitHub environment secret FLY_API_TOKEN for that environment (production: a required reviewer approves the change).
Verify by re-running the deploy workflow for staging (or the production workflow with approval).
Revoke the old token: `fly tokens list -a hs-core-<env>` then `fly tokens revoke <id>`.
Add a line to the rotation log.
github-env-secret: Create the new value at its source (provider dashboard, `fly tokens create`, Sentry settings) scoped to this environment only.
Update the GitHub environment secret for that environment (Settings > Environments > <env>); production requires a reviewer.
Re-run the workflow that uses it and confirm it succeeds.
Revoke the old value at its source.
Add a line to the rotation log.
service-account: In the Firebase/Google Cloud console create a new service-account key (JSON) for THIS environment's Firebase project; keep the old key active.
Set it on the core service (`fly secrets import -a hs-core-<env>` with `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON=<single-line JSON>` on stdin from a mode-600 file, then delete the local file).
Verify by sending a test push to a staging device.
Delete the OLD key in the service-account page (this is the revoke step).
Add a line to the rotation log.
apns-key: In the Apple Developer account create a new APNs auth key (.p8); Apple allows two active keys.
Upload it to the Firebase project for THIS environment (Project settings > Cloud Messaging > APNs authentication key) and record the key id.
Verify with a test push to an iOS TestFlight build.
Revoke the old APNs key in the Apple Developer account.
Add a line to the rotation log. Keep the .p8 file out of the repo and out of chat.
signing-credential: Generate or request the replacement in the store console (Play Console > Setup > App signing > request upload key reset; Apple Developer > Certificates; App Store Connect > Users and Access > Integrations > Keys), keeping the old one valid until the new build is verified.
Store the new material only in the Codemagic secure variable group (or the store console) for the production release; never in the repo, chat or a laptop file that outlives the step.
Verify: run a Codemagic build and upload one internal-track (Play) or TestFlight (App Store) build signed with the new credential.
Revoke the OLD credential in the same console (this is the revoke step; on a leak do it as soon as step 3 passes).
Add a line to the rotation log (date, who, credential name; no values). Draft procedure until M01 sets up Codemagic.
admin-cookie-secret: Generate a new value locally (`openssl rand -hex 32`, 32+ characters); never paste it into chat or an issue.

Set the same value on every admin instance of THIS environment in the admin host's environment settings (the host is chosen with F06 deployment, owner-blocked) and redeploy all instances together; a mix of old and new values breaks pending-MFA verification across instances.
Verify: sign in to the staging admin with MFA end to end (production: with the owner's account in a quiet window).
Discard the old value everywhere; only in-flight pending-MFA cookies (10 minutes) were invalidated.
Add a line to the rotation log (date, who, secret name, environment; no values).

entries.name: APPWRITE_API_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Read/write every row, set user labels, write files in one environment's Appwrite project. Cannot change schema. Production leak = full read/write of live family and child data.

entries.name: APPWRITE_API_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Change schema, buckets and functions of one environment's project; no user access. Production key lacks databases.write.

entries.name: JOB_TICK_SECRET
entries.blast_radius: Forge a job tick: trigger payout, reminder and expiry jobs on demand in one environment (jobs are idempotent, so impact is load and timing, not duplicate payments).

entries.name: JOB_TICK_SECRET
entries.blast_radius: Same value as the core service copy; leak lets an attacker sign ticks.

entries.name: MOMO_COLLECTION_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Call MoMo Collections as us (request payments). Production: live money movement into our account.

entries.name: MOMO_COLLECTION_API_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Authenticate to MoMo Collections with our API user. Production: request payments from parents' wallets in our name.

entries.name: MOMO_DISBURSEMENT_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Call MoMo Disbursements as us. Production: pay out money from our wallet.

entries.name: MOMO_DISBURSEMENT_API_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Authenticate to MoMo Disbursements. Production: send payouts to arbitrary numbers; highest financial blast radius.

entries.name: AIRTEL_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.blast_radius: Airtel Money OAuth client secret. Phase 2. Production: collections and payouts through Airtel.

entries.name: CARD_GATEWAY_SECRET_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Card gateway secret key (provider TBD, see memory.md questions). Production: charge and refund cards.

entries.name: CARD_GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.blast_radius: Forge payment-confirmed webhooks if leaked (provider TBD). Production: mark unpaid plans as paid.

entries.name: FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
entries.blast_radius: Send push notifications to any device registered in one environment's Firebase project (phishing risk), no data read.

entries.name: APNS_AUTH_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Send iOS pushes for our bundle id via Apple. Held in the Firebase console, not in our repo, Fly or GitHub.

entries.name: RESEND_API_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Send email as our domain (receipts, safeguarding notices); phishing and reputation risk. Restrict to sending only (ADR 0005).

entries.name: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.blast_radius: Forge delivery and bounce events.

entries.name: AFRICASTALKING_API_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Send OTP and other SMS on our account (cost and phishing risk).

entries.name: GOOGLE_MAPS_SERVER_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Run Routes/Distance Matrix on our bill. Restrict by API and, where possible, by IP; budget alert on.

entries.name: SENTRY_DSN
entries.blast_radius: Write-only: submit fake events to our Sentry project. Low severity; rotate by creating a new client key and deleting the old one.

entries.name: SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN
entries.blast_radius: Upload source maps and manage releases in Sentry; scoped to project:releases only.

entries.name: FLY_API_TOKEN
entries.blast_radius: Deploy and read secrets of one Fly app. Must be an app-scoped deploy token, never an org token. Production token sits in the protected production environment.

entries.name: GOOGLE_MAPS_ANDROID_KEY
entries.restriction: Restrict in Google Cloud to the Android package name + signing SHA-1 and to Places/Maps SDK only; daily quota cap and budget alert.
entries.notes: Public by design; ships in the app bundle.

entries.name: GOOGLE_MAPS_IOS_KEY
entries.restriction: Restrict in Google Cloud to the iOS bundle id and to Places/Maps SDK only; daily quota cap and budget alert.
entries.notes: Public by design; ships in the app bundle.

entries.name: SENTRY_DSN_APP
entries.restriction: Sentry client key with inbound filters, rate limit and allowed origins; scrub personal data before send (SR 10).
entries.notes: DSN is write-only and public by design.

entries.name: SENTRY_DSN_APP
entries.restriction: Sentry client key with inbound filters, rate limit and allowed origins; scrub personal data before send (SR 10).
entries.notes: DSN is write-only and public by design.

entries.name: HS_ENV
entries.notes: Selects validation strictness; deployed environments fail fast when required variables are missing.

entries.name: HS_DEBUG
entries.notes: Must be false in production (enforced at startup).

entries.name: APPWRITE_ENDPOINT
entries.notes: Must be https and not localhost in deployed environments.

entries.name: APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID
entries.notes: One Appwrite project per environment (SR 4). Public identifier, also in app builds.

entries.name: JOB_ALERT_AFTER_FAILURES
entries.notes: F04: consecutive job failures before an alert.

entries.name: CORE_SERVICE_URL
entries.notes: F04: function variable; public URL of the core app for that environment.

entries.name: ADMIN_ENV
entries.notes: F06: unknown or missing maps to Local, never Production.

entries.name: MOMO_COLLECTION_API_USER
entries.notes: Provider-issued user id (not a secret by itself).

entries.name: MOMO_DISBURSEMENT_API_USER
entries.notes: Provider-issued user id (not a secret by itself).

entries.name: APPWRITE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S
entries.notes: F04: seconds to wait for the TCP connect to Appwrite.

entries.name: APPWRITE_READ_TIMEOUT_S
entries.notes: F04: seconds to wait for an Appwrite response.

entries.name: PLAY_UPLOAD_KEYSTORE
entries.blast_radius: Sign app bundles as us for upload to Play. Play App Signing holds the real app signing key, so a leaked upload key can be reset through Play support; still a release-integrity risk.

entries.name: PLAY_UPLOAD_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD
entries.blast_radius: With the keystore file, signs uploads to Play. Stored as a Codemagic secure variable; never committed.

entries.name: IOS_DISTRIBUTION_CERTIFICATE
entries.blast_radius: Sign iOS builds as the company; Apple certificates expire after 1 year. Revoke in the Apple Developer account on a leak.

entries.name: IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILES
entries.blast_radius: Profiles tie the certificate to the app ids; regenerated whenever the certificate is replaced. Low impact alone.

entries.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_API_KEY
entries.blast_radius: Upload builds and manage TestFlight and metadata in App Store Connect with the role given to the key. Use the minimum role (App Manager or Developer).

entries.name: CODEMAGIC_SECURE_VARIABLES
entries.blast_radius: Group of per-environment Codemagic variables holding signing material and store API keys (public client keys are not secret). Leak lets an attacker build and publish as us.

entries.name: ADMIN_COOKIE_SECRET
entries.downtime_note: Rotating invalidates in-flight pending-MFA cookies only (10 minute lifetime): an admin mid-login restarts the sign-in. Established sessions are Appwrite sessions and are unaffected.
entries.blast_radius: Forge the signed pending-MFA cookie of the admin sign-in, skipping the cookie-binding step (the Appwrite password and MFA challenge are still required for a real session). Must be 32+ random characters and identical on every admin instance of the environment.
